newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post - April 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post - April 16.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following items on its front page on April 16:

WASHINGTON - The FBI crime laboratory produced scientifically flawed report and inaccurate testimony in several major cases, including the World Trade Center and Oklahoma City bombings, according to a Justice Department report.

WASHINGTON - For the past several months consumers have been snapping up new cars, furniture, airline tickets and all sorts of other items, but despite the spending spree and an overall strong economy, the prices Americans pay aren't rising much.
WASHINGTON - States may not force political candidates to take drug tests, the Supreme Court ruled, striking down a Georgia law as mere symbolism.
WASHINGTON - After five previous convictions, a visibly frustrated U.S. magistrate judge sentenced an Arlington, Va. lawyer to five months in prison for drunk driving.

WASHINGTON - As crack cocaine, AIDS and other modern-day plagues continue to leave growing numbers of parents unable to care for their children, child welfare workers are increasingly turning to the extended family -- grandmothers, aunts, uncles, cousins and even close friends -- for help.

SEOUL - Businessman John K. H. Lee, who donated $250,000 to the Democratic National Committee, is under investigation by authorities in South Korea for an alleged scheme to lure investors into a U.S. venture by scamming them into believing that he had friends in high places in Washington.
